items.q: The Traver et al classification is a:
items.exp: Traver et al classification: histological classification. (Book p816)

items.q: Match the following Traver class to its feature — 1) I  2) II  3) III  4) IV … A) Nodular sclerosis (KW lesions)  B) Advanced diabetic glomerulosclerosis  C) GBM thickening (earliest finding)  D) Mesangial expansion (m/c)
items.exp: I: GBM thickening (earliest); II: mesangial expansion (m/c 90%; afferent & efferent hyalinosis); III: nodular sclerosis (KW lesions, 50% pts, most specific); IV: advanced diabetic glomerulosclerosis. (Book p816)

items.q: Mesangial expansion (class II) is the m/c pattern in what share?
KW lesions (class III) appear in only what share of patients, and are the most specific?
items.exp: Class III: nodular sclerosis (KW lesions - Kimmelstiel wilson) only 50% pts, most specific. (Book p816)

items.q: Fill up: The KW lesions of class III are named after Kimmelstiel and ______.
All but one are Traver classes. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Traver classes I-IV: GBM thickening, mesangial expansion, nodular sclerosis (KW), advanced diabetic glomerulosclerosis. (Book p816)

items.q: Class II also includes which arteriolar change?
opts: Intimal fibrosis of the vessel wall
items.exp: Class II: mesangial expansion (m/c 90%) (afferent & efferent hyalinosis). (Book p816)

items.q: The nodular kidney diseases in the note are:
opts: Diabetes (KW nodules), MPGN, lichen deposition diseases, amyloidosis, smokers
IgA nephropathy, FSGS (proliferative type), lupus nephritis, transplant
Alport, thin basement membrane, minimal change disease
Amyloidosis alone, without other nodular causes
items.exp: Nodular kidney diseases: diabetes (KW nodules); MPGN (membrano proliferative glomerulonephritis); lichen deposition diseases; amyloidosis; smokers. (Book p816)

items.q: All but one are nodular kidney diseases on the note. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Note list: diabetes, MPGN, lichen deposition diseases, amyloidosis, smokers. (Book p816)

items.q: Diabetic nephropathy is also known as:
items.exp: Diabetic nephropathy: AKA albuminuric DKD. (Book p816)

items.q: The first criterion for diabetic nephropathy is:
opts: Microscopic hematuria with RBC casts on microscopy
Oliguria with rising creatinine over days (AKI pattern)
Hyperkalemia with metabolic acidosis and hyperphosphatemia
items.exp: Criteria all of: proteinuria (albuminuria): nephrotic range without syndrome. (Book p816)

items.q: Diabetic nephropathy criteria include micro- or macro-hematuria.
opts: False — the criteria state no micro/macro hematuria
False — hematuria is required for the diagnosis
True, but only in children and adolescents
